docs.title: 🧺 Cobblemon Picnic
docs.text:
Cobblemon Picnic is a Cobblemon add-on that turns spawn-hunting into a cozy picnic. Place a Picnic Table, right-click it, and it despawns the nearby wild Pokémon and forces a fresh "maximized" natural respawn around you — a spawn re-roller for hunting shinies or a specific species without roaming the world.

It's also a social station: sit on the benches for a shiny bonus, care for your Pokémon, store snacks in baskets, and summon trainers to battle.

Requirements

Minecraft 1.21.1 · Fabric or NeoForge · Cobblemon 1.7.x. Fabric also needs Fabric API + Fabric Language Kotlin; NeoForge needs Architectury API + Kotlin for Forge. Cloth Config (+ Mod Menu on Fabric) is optional — the in-game settings screen only.

docs.title: What can it do?
docs.text:
• Spawn re-rolling — despawn wild Pokémon and force a fresh batch around you, on demand.
  • Four table tiers — Basic, Camping, Glamping, and the underwater-only Diving table.
  • Shiny aura — sit together to raise shiny odds, with a particle ring and a HUD buff.
  • Interactions & items — wash & play with Pokémon, store bread in baskets, bias spawns with snacks.
  • Battle Seeker — a rare item that summons RCT trainers from a Glamping table.
  • Commands & Configuration — full in-game tuning and live statistics.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
• Download: Modrinth (Fabric & NeoForge) · CurseForge
  • Bugs & ideas: report them in the community Discord — they're forwarded straight to the project's issue tracker.

New here? Start with Getting Started.

License

Custom — "If you make money, I make money." Free to use and share for free; commercial use requires a revenue-share agreement with the author. Table/bench models & textures were adapted from CobbleFurnies and Handcrafted.

docs.title: Battle Seeker
docs.text: The Battle Seeker turns a Glamping table into a trainer-battle generator.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Place a Battle Seeker in a Glamping table's fuel slot. Now, when you re-roll, instead of (or alongside) wild spawns, the table summons an RCT trainer for you to battle. The Battle Seeker is not consumed — it stays in the slot so you can keep challenging trainers.

The summoned trainer's level is matched to your party, adjustable in configuration:

Setting Meaning spawnappropriatelvltrainer <true\|false> Scale the trainer to your party's level. trainerlevelgap <int> Level offset applied on top of the match (e.g. make them a bit tougher).

docs.title: How to get one
docs.text: The Battle Seeker has no crafting recipe. It's a rare loot item found in world chests — keep exploring structures and you may find one.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Needs RCT

The trainer spawn uses Radical Cobblemon Trainers (RCT). If RCT isn't installed, the Battle Seeker simply does nothing — the rest of the table works normally.

Glamping only

Only the Glamping tier exposes the Battle Seeker slot. Lower tiers use that slot for bread fuel instead.

docs.title: /cobblemonpicnicstats
docs.text:
Available to everyone. Shows a summary of picnic activity:

  • Total re-rolls, Pokémon spawned / despawned
  • Shinies found (with ratio), legendaries / mythicals
  • Snacks consumed, distinct species
  • Most common and rarest species
/cobblemonpicnicstats          # show the summary
/cobblemonpicnicstats reset    # (operator) clear the aggregates

Statistics persist in config/cobblemon_picnic_stats.json (aggregates) and config/cobblemon_picnic_events.jsonl (a granular per-re-roll log).

docs.title: /cobblemonpicnicconfig
docs.text:
Operator only. Read and change settings live.

/cobblemonpicnicconfig get                  # print current settings
/cobblemonpicnicconfig reload               # reload config file from disk
/cobblemonpicnicconfig reset                # restore defaults
/cobblemonpicnicconfig set <param> <value>  # change one setting

docs.title: Settings you can set
docs.text:
Parameter Value What it does spawncap <basic\|camping\|glamping\|diving> int Max Pokémon per re-roll for that tier. fuelcost <tier> int Bread consumed per re-roll for that tier (defaults 7 / 5 / 3 / 3). rerollcooldown 0–3600 Seconds between re-rolls (per-table and per-player). Default 5. 0 disables. tmteachchance 0..1 Chance per re-roll a party Pokémon teaches another a legal move. Default 0.05. 0 disables. light 0–15 Light level emitted by the table. aurabase 0..1 Base shiny boost per occupied seat. auramax 0..1 Cap on the total shiny boost. shinyaura true/false Master switch for the Shiny Aura. deployonsit true/false Whether sitting deploys the seat behavior. actiondistance number Interaction range for picnic actions. washfriendship int Friendship gained from washing. washrequirestable true/false Require a nearby table to wash. slimeballfriendship int Friendship gained from playing. slimeballbreakchance 0..1 Chance the slime ball breaks when playing. slimeballrequirestable true/false Require a nearby table to play. spawnappropriatelvltrainer true/false Scale Battle Seeker trainers to your level. trainerlevelgap int Level offset for summoned trainers. protectshiny true/false Re-roll keeps shiny wild Pokémon instead of despawning them. Default off. protectlegendary true/false Re-roll keeps legendary wild Pokémon. Default off. protectmythical true/false Re-roll keeps mythical wild Pokémon. Default off. protectultrabeast true/false Re-roll keeps Ultra Beast wild Pokémon. Default off. disableseatedaggro true/false While someone is seated, hostile mobs flee the table. Default on. seatedrepelradius 0–128 How far (blocks) the seated mob-repulsion reaches. Default 30.

Peaceful picnic & rare protection

The four protect… toggles are opt-in (default off) and granular — turn on only the rarities you want the re-roll to spare. disableseatedaggro is on by default: sit at a table and hostile mobs within seatedrepelradius blocks lose their target and run away, like a creeper fleeing a cat.

Note

Seat counts are not configurable — they're fixed per tier. On a dedicated server use these commands; the Mod Menu screen only edits the local client config.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Cobblemon Picnic can be tuned three ways: a config file, in-game commands, and an optional Mod Menu screen.

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
Runtime settings live in:

config/cobblemon_picnic.json

Edit it with a text editor, then apply your changes with /cobblemonpicnicconfig reload (no restart needed). Statistics are stored separately in config/cobblemon_picnic_stats.json and config/cobblemon_picnic_events.jsonl.

docs.title: In-game commands
docs.text:
The fastest way to change a single value is the /cobblemonpicnicconfig command — see the Commands page for the full parameter list. Highlights:

  • Spawns: spawncap <tier>, fuelcost <tier>, rerollcooldown <seconds>
  • Shiny aura: shinyaura, aurabase, auramax
  • Care: washfriendship, slimeballfriendship, slimeballbreakchance
  • Party fun: tmteachchance (rare TM cross-teaching on re-roll)
  • Battle Seeker: spawnappropriatelvltrainer, trainerlevelgap
  • Re-roll protection: protectshiny, protectlegendary, protectmythical, protectultrabeast
  • Peaceful picnic: disableseatedaggro (on by default), seatedrepelradius
  • Misc: light, actiondistance, deployonsit

docs.title: Mod Menu screen
docs.text:
With Mod Menu + Cloth Config installed, open Mods → Cobblemon Picnic → Settings (the gear button) to edit the same values in a GUI.

Mod Menu edits the local config

On a dedicated server, the Mod Menu screen only changes your client's file — use /cobblemonpicnicconfig set ... to change the server's settings for everyone.

docs.title: Defaults reference
docs.text:
Tier Spawn cap Fuel/re-roll Radius Seats Basic 5 7 32 2 Camping 8 5 48 3 Glamping 12 3 64 4 Diving 12 3 64 4

Other notable defaults: re-roll cooldown 5 s (per-table + per-player), party TM cross-teach chance 0.05 (5%).

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Does re-rolling despawn my own Pokémon?

No. The despawn step skips any Pokémon that has an owner (yours or another player's) and any tethered/busy Pokémon. Only wild Pokémon in range are cleared.

Why won't my table place?

The table is a 3×2 multiblock and deploys in front of you. All six cells need to be free. The Diving table additionally requires being underwater.

I broke one block and the whole table disappeared.

That's intended — a Picnic Table is a single multiblock structure. Breaking any cell breaks the whole table and returns the item. (Place tables so their footprints don't overlap.)

The re-roll says I'm out of fuel.

Basic and Camping tables consume bread per re-roll. Put bread in the fuel slot or place a Picnic Basket with bread nearby. Glamping and Diving are free.

How do I increase shiny odds?

Sit on the benches — each occupied seat adds to the Shiny Aura, which boosts your next re-roll. Bring friends for a bigger bonus. It can be tuned or disabled in config.

The Battle Seeker isn't doing anything.

It only works in a Glamping table's slot, and it needs Radical Cobblemon Trainers (RCT) installed to spawn the trainer. See Battle Seeker.

Where do I find the Battle Seeker?

It has no recipe — it's a rare chest loot item. Keep looting structures.

Does this work on NeoForge?

Yes! Since 1.25.0, Cobblemon Picnic ships for both Fabric and NeoForge (Minecraft 1.21.1) with the same features on each. Grab the NeoForge build from Modrinth or CurseForge — it needs Architectury API + Kotlin for Forge.

Found a bug or have an idea?

Post it in the community Discord's #bugs or #features channels — new posts (with their text and attachments) are picked up automatically and filed into the project's issue tracker, and you'll get a reply in your thread when a fix ships.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Cobblemon Picnic runs on Fabric and NeoForge for Minecraft 1.21.1.

  1. Install your loader for Minecraft 1.21.1: Fabric Loader or NeoForge 21.1.x.
  2. Put these mods in your mods/ folder:
    • Cobblemon Picnic (Modrinth / CurseForge)
    • Cobblemon 1.7.x
    • Fabric: Fabric API + Fabric Language Kotlin
    • NeoForge: Architectury API + Kotlin for Forge
  3. (Optional) Cloth Config for the in-game settings screen (plus Mod Menu on Fabric — on NeoForge the screen opens from the mods list's Config button).

Server vs. client

The mod runs on both. On a dedicated server, use the commands to configure it (the Mod Menu screen only edits the local client config).

docs.title: Your first table
docs.text:
1. Craft a Picnic Table. Tables are crafted from a cloth (any of the 16 dye colors) over a bench of any wood — the table renders in that exact color/wood combo. See Picnic Tables → Crafting.
  2. Place it on open, flat ground. The table is a 3×2 multiblock that deploys in front of you, with the table column centered — so face the direction you want it and place.
  3. Add fuel. Open the table (the GUI) and drop bread into the fuel slot, or place a Picnic Basket with bread nearby.
  4. Re-roll! Right-click the center (table) cells to despawn the surrounding wild Pokémon and roll a fresh batch. The slider in the GUI sets how many spawn (capped by tier).

Placement needs room

The footprint is 3 wide × 2 deep. If the cells are blocked, the table won't place. Leave a clear area so spawns have room to appear.

docs.title: What next?
docs.text:
• Bring friends and sit on the benches to boost shiny odds.
  • Upgrade toward Glamping for the biggest radius and the Battle Seeker slot.
  • Going underwater? Build a Diving table.

docs.title: Interactions & Items
docs.text: Beyond re-rolling, the picnic is a place to care for your Pokémon and manage supplies.

docs.title: Pokémon care (Cobblemon interaction wheel)
docs.text:
Point at one of your Pokémon and open Cobblemon's interaction wheel — Cobblemon Picnic adds two options:

Wash 🧽Play 🟢

Use a wet sponge to wash a Pokémon → +friendship. The sponge is consumed. By default this requires being near a table (configurable via washrequirestable). Friendship gained is set by washfriendship.

Use a slime ball to play fetch → a throw / fetch / return animation, +friendship, and a small chance the ball breaks. There's a 0.5 s cooldown between plays. Tunables: slimeballfriendship, slimeballbreakchance, slimeballrequirestable.

docs.title: Picnic Baskets
docs.text:
Picnic Baskets are placeable furniture available in every apricorn color.

  • Place one on the ground like a block.
  • Store bread inside it.
  • A nearby table pulls bread from baskets to fuel its re-rolls — so you can keep a basket stocked next to your setup instead of refilling the fuel slot.

docs.title: poke_snack bias
docs.text:
If a seasoned poke_snack (a Cobblemon snack item with spawn influence) is on the ground near a table when you re-roll:

  • The re-roll respects the snack's spawn influence, biasing what appears.
  • One bite is consumed from the closest snack each time.

This lets you steer a re-roll toward the kinds of Pokémon a given snack attracts.

docs.title: Customization & misc
docs.text:
• Colors & woods — tables come in 16 cloth colors × wood types; baskets in every apricorn color. All variants are in the Creative inventory.
  • Flammable — tables burn like wood planks if exposed to fire.

Tip

Friendship-building at the picnic stacks with normal Cobblemon mechanics — a good way to evolve friendship-based Pokémon while you hunt.

docs.title: Picnic Tables
docs.text: Picnic Tables are the core block of the mod. Each is a 3×2 multiblock: the center column holds the table cells (re-roll + GUI), and the side cells are benches you can sit on, up to the tier's seat cap. Leftover side cells stay empty.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
Tier Spawn cap Radius Seats Fuel / re-roll Notes Basic 5 32 2 7 bread Entry tier Camping 8 48 3 5 bread Cheaper fuel, bigger Glamping 12 64 4 3 bread Unlocks the Battle Seeker slot Diving 12 64 4 3 bread Placed underwater only
  • Spawn cap — the maximum Pokémon a single re-roll can spawn (and the GUI slider's max).
  • Radius — how far around the table wild Pokémon are despawned and re-rolled.
  • Seats — how many benches the footprint provides (seat counts are fixed per tier, not configurable).
  • Fuel — bread consumed per re-roll, on a 7 / 5 / 3 / 3 curve (cheaper as tiers improve). Bread comes from the table's fuel slot or from a nearby Picnic Basket. The per-tier cost is configurable (fuelcost <tier>).

Upgrading

You can upgrade a table to a higher tier via crafting — the recipe keeps the cloth color and bench wood you originally used, so your table stays the same style.

docs.title: Crafting
docs.text:
Tables are crafted from a cloth on top of a bench:

  • Cloth — any of the 16 dye colors sets the tablecloth color.
  • Bench — any of the supported wood types sets the frame wood.

The result renders in that exact color × wood combination, using the mod's own models and textures (no other furniture mod required). Every color/wood variant is available in the Creative inventory.

Diving table

The Diving table can only be placed underwater. Try to place it in air and it won't deploy.

docs.title: Placement & orientation
docs.text:
• The table deploys in front of you when you place it, with the table column centered on where you aim. It orients to your facing — the "wide" axis runs left-to-right relative to you.
  • The structure is one block tall. Benches sit on the sides; the center is the functional table.
  • Breaking any cell breaks the whole structure and returns the table item.

Don't place two tables touching

Give each table its own footprint. Overlapping structures can interfere with each other's cells.

docs.title: Reporting Bugs & Features
docs.text: Found a bug, or have an idea? You don't need a GitHub account — just post in our Discord, and your message is turned into a tracked issue automatically (and you get credited!).

docs.title: Where to post
docs.text:
Channel For #bugs something broken or behaving wrong #features an idea, request, or improvement

Within a few minutes, a bot reads your message, opens an issue on the project's tracker, and adds a ✅ reaction to your message so you know it was logged.

docs.title: Writing a good bug report
docs.text:
A little detail goes a long way. Try to include:

  • What happened vs. what you expected.
  • Steps to reproduce it (what were you doing?).
  • Your versions — Minecraft, Cobblemon, and Cobblemon Picnic.
  • Other mods that might be involved, and a screenshot or log if you have one.

Example

Placing a Diving table underwater near coral crashes the client. MC 1.21.1, Cobblemon 1.7.3, Picnic 1.24.0. Happens every time; log attached. Only other furniture mod is Handcrafted.

docs.title: Writing a good feature request
docs.text:
• What you'd like and why it would help your playstyle.
  • If it's a tweak to something that exists, say what's missing today.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
• Your post becomes an issue labelled bug or enhancement (plus discord).
  • You're added to the Community Credits page.
  • Progress happens on the tracker and ships in a future release — watch the changelog.

Thank you for helping make the mod better! 💚

docs.title: Shiny Aura
docs.text:
Picnics are better with friends — and more friends means more shinies.

Sit on a table's benches and each occupied seat raises the shiny odds for everyone seated — for the table's next re-roll and for wild Pokémon that spawn naturally around you while you sit. The more people seated, the stronger the Shiny Aura.

docs.title: How it shows
docs.text:
• A ring of particles hovers above the table while the aura is active.
  • Anyone in range gets a "Shiny Aura" buff in their HUD, with a numeric level that scales with how many people are seated (it reads at least 1 at one seat).

docs.title: How to sit
docs.text: Right-click a bench cell (a side seat) with an empty hand to sit. Sneak or move to stand up. Seats are invisible mounts — you'll snap neatly onto the bench.

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
The aura is fully configurable (see Configuration):

Setting Meaning shinyaura <true\|false> Master on/off switch for the whole feature. aurabase <0..1> Base shiny boost contributed per occupied seat. auramax <0..1> Cap on the total boost, no matter how many are seated.

When the boost applies

The Shiny Aura is a per-player odds floor that stays live the whole time you're seated at a table (it clears about a second after you stand up). While it's live it improves the odds of any shiny roll Cobblemon attributes to you — that means the table's re-roll and the natural wild spawns that appear around you as you sit. Triggering a re-roll also grants the floor to the player who triggered it for that roll. It only ever raises your odds — it never lowers a boost already coming from a Shiny Charm or a higher server shiny rate.

docs.title: Spawn Re-rolling
docs.text:
The headline feature. Right-click the center (table) cells and the table will:

  1. Despawn nearby wild Pokémon within the tier's radius — but never owned/tethered Pokémon (yours and other players' stay safe).
  2. Force a fresh "maximized" natural respawn around the table, using Cobblemon's own spawner at a boosted density so you get a full batch immediately.

This lets you re-roll the local spawns on demand — ideal for shiny hunting or fishing for a specific species without wandering the world.

docs.title: How many spawn?
docs.text: Open the table's GUI and use the slider to choose how many Pokémon a re-roll spawns, up to the tier's spawn cap (Basic 5 → Glamping/Diving 12). The re-roll runs several spawner passes and stops early once it has placed enough or a pass yields nothing.

docs.title: Fuel
docs.text:
Each re-roll costs bread, depending on tier:

Tier Bread per re-roll Basic 7 Camping 5 Glamping 3 Diving 3

The cost follows a 7 / 5 / 3 / 3 curve — cheaper as tiers improve. Bread can come from the table's fuel slot or from a nearby placed Picnic Basket — the table will pull from baskets automatically. Out of bread? The table tells you and the re-roll is cancelled. Each per-tier cost is configurable via fuelcost <tier> (see Configuration).

docs.title: Cooldown
docs.text: To stop a table being spammed, each re-roll starts a cooldown (default 5 seconds). It's enforced both per-table and per-player — whichever is still counting down blocks the re-roll, so you can't dodge it by hopping between tables. A blocked attempt shows a short actionbar countdown and costs no bread. Change it with rerollcooldown <seconds> (0 disables the wait).

docs.title: Party TM teaching
docs.text: Every re-roll has a small chance (5% by default) that one of your party Pokémon teaches another party member one of its moves — a little picnic bonding. A Pokémon only ever learns a move it is actually able to learn (its normal learnset / TM compatibility), so it never gains an illegal move; if all four slots are full, one move is swapped out. Tune or disable it with tmteachchance <0..1>.

docs.title: Snack bias
docs.text:
If a seasoned poke_snack is nearby when you re-roll, the spawn respects that snack's spawn influence (so you can bias toward what the snack attracts) and consumes one bite of the closest snack. See Interactions & Items → Snacks.

Owned Pokémon are protected

The despawn step explicitly skips Pokémon with an owner. You can leave your party out (or a pasture nearby) and re-roll freely.
